1303.content: Connect an Azure subscription with a service principal, prepare the Blob state container, and see what OrkStage creates on Container Apps and Flexible Server.

1312.content:
The Azure adapter is covered by unit tests and its OpenTofu modules pass `tofu validate`. It has
not been verified against a live subscription yet.

1313.content:
OrkStage creates Azure resources with OpenTofu (`hashicorp/azurerm` 5.x) in a throwaway runner
container, one isolated state per resource, kept in a Blob container in your own subscription.
Health, secrets, logs and the restart action use the Azure Resource Manager, Key Vault and Log
Analytics REST APIs.

1314.content:
Every resource gets its own resource group (`<name>-rg`), so destroying it removes everything it
created.

1315.content:
| Template resource | Capability       | What gets created                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `network`         | `vnet` (default) | Virtual network with a delegated Container Apps subnet, a delegated PostgreSQL subnet and a private endpoint subnet, optional NAT gateway, Log Analytics workspace, the Container Apps environment that the services of the network share, private DNS zone for Redis |

1316.content:
| Template resource           | Capability                 | What gets created                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `compute.container-service` | `container-apps` (default) | Container app with a user assigned identity, external ingress when public, CPU scale rule from `autoscaling`, Key Vault backed secrets for dependencies, Storage Blob Data Contributor on dependent storage accounts. Its own environment when there is no network. |

1317.content:
| Template resource     | Capability                  | What gets created                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `database.postgresql` | `flexible-server` (default) | Flexible server with private access through the delegated subnet and a private DNS zone, database `app`, Key Vault holding the generated credentials |

1318.content:
| Template resource | Capability                | What gets created                                                                                |
| ----------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `cache.redis`     | `managed-redis` (default) | Azure Managed Redis (private endpoint when there is a network), Key Vault holding the access key |

1319.content:
| Template resource | Capability               | What gets created                                                                                                     |
| ----------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `object-storage`  | `blob-storage` (default) | Storage account with one container, versioning, soft delete, lifecycle rules for `retentionDays` and the archive tier |

1320.content:
| Template resource | Capability                         | What gets created                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ingress`         | `container-apps-ingress` (default) | Nothing: each service keeps the HTTPS address of the built in Container Apps ingress |

1321.content:
| Template resource | Capability   | What gets created                                                                           |
| ----------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ingress`         | `front-door` | Front Door Standard profile and endpoint with one route and origin group per routed service |

1322.content:
Services receive `<ID>_HOST`, `<ID>_PORT`, `<ID>_URL`, `<ID>_BUCKET` and `<ID>_ENDPOINT` for each
dependency, and `<ID>_CREDENTIALS` with the JSON credentials from Key Vault (`username`,
`password`, `host`, `port`, `database`, `url`). `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` points Azure SDKs at the app's
identity for storage access.

1323.content:
PostgreSQL passwords are generated with an ephemeral resource and written through write only
attributes, so they never enter OpenTofu state. Module outputs carry only the Key Vault secret id
(`secret_ref`).

1324.content:
Production resources get Key Vault purge protection, a `CanNotDelete` lock on databases and
storage accounts, and resource groups that refuse to be deleted while they still hold resources.

1325.content:
| `config` field | Required | Meaning                                        |
| -------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `tenantId`     | yes      | Directory (tenant) id of the service principal |

1326.content:
| `config` field   | Required | Meaning                                  |
| ---------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `subscriptionId` | yes      | Subscription that receives the resources |

1327.content:
| `config` field | Required | Meaning                                          |
| -------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `clientId`     | yes      | Application (client) id of the service principal |

1328.content:
| `config` field       | Required | Meaning                                     |
| -------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `stateResourceGroup` | yes      | Resource group of the state storage account |

1329.content:
| `config` field        | Required | Meaning                                                                  |
| --------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `stateStorageAccount` | yes      | Storage account for OpenTofu state, 3 to 24 lowercase letters and digits |

1330.content:
| `config` field   | Required | Meaning                                                   |
| ---------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `stateContainer` | no       | Blob container for state. Defaults to `orkstage-tfstate`. |

1331.content:
OrkStage signs in with a service principal and a client secret. The secret behind `credentialRef`
is a JSON object:

1332.content:
A plain string is also accepted and is taken as `clientSecret`. The values reach OpenTofu only as
runner environment variables (`ARM_TENANT_ID`, `ARM_CLIENT_ID`, `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET`,
`ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`). Workload identity federation, with no stored secret, is planned.

1333.content:
Run these once per subscription with the Azure CLI, signed in as someone who can create role
assignments.

1334.content: OrkStage never creates the state container. Validation reports it as missing until it exists.

1335.content:
| Role        | Scope        | Why                                                                    |
| ----------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Contributor | subscription | Create resource groups and every resource, register resource providers |

1336.content:
| Role                      | Scope        | Why                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| User Access Administrator | subscription | Role assignments (Key Vault and storage access for apps, Key Vault access for OrkStage) and production delete locks |

1337.content:
| Role                          | Scope                 | Why                           |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Storage Blob Data Contributor | state storage account | Read and write OpenTofu state |

1338.content:
Owner on the subscription covers the first two. OrkStage gives itself Key Vault Secrets Officer on
the vaults it creates, so it can write generated credentials and read them back for resources on
other providers.

1339.content:
Resource providers are registered on first use (`Microsoft.App`, `Microsoft.OperationalInsights`,
`Microsoft.ManagedIdentity`, `Microsoft.Network`, `Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL`, `Microsoft.Cache`,
`Microsoft.KeyVault`, `Microsoft.Storage`, `Microsoft.Cdn`). Validation warns about the ones that
are not registered yet.

1340.content:
Regions are Azure locations such as `eastus`, `brazilsouth` or `westeurope`. List the ones the
target may use in `allowedRegions`.

1341.content:
| Capability       | Action    | Parameters | Effect                                                                        |
| ---------------- | --------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `container-apps` | `restart` | none       | Restarts the active revision of the container app; its replicas are recreated |

1342.content: Logs come from the `ContainerAppConsoleLogs_CL` table of the Log Analytics workspace.

1343.content:
Container Apps run on the Consumption profile: up to 4 vCPU and 8 GiB per replica, and memory
is always twice the vCPU, so the size follows the larger of `cpu` and `memoryMiB`.

1344.content: Images must be pullable without credentials. Private registries are not wired yet.

1345.content: The CPU scale rule cannot wake an app from zero, so autoscaled apps keep at least one replica.

1346.content:
PostgreSQL backups cannot be turned off (minimum 7 days). High availability needs the General
Purpose tier, so `micro` and `small` move to `GP_Standard_D2ds_v5` when HA is requested.

1347.content:
Private PostgreSQL needs a network in the same placement slot. With `publicAccess`, the server
accepts connections from Azure services only.

1348.content:
Managed Redis replication is on or off: any `replicas` above zero, or production, turns high
availability on.

1349.content:
Blob Storage has shared keys turned off. Clients use Microsoft Entra identities, so the storage
account hands no keys to resources on other providers.

1350.content:
Credentials published outside Azure Key Vault (another provider's `secret_ref`) are copied into
Container Apps secrets at deploy time and reach the app as `<ID>_USERNAME`, `<ID>_PASSWORD` and so
on (see plan and cost).

1351.content:
Front Door routes are created before the apps behind them. A route answers once its service has
been deployed and joined its origin group. Only public apps can be origins.

1352.content:
Zone redundancy of the Container Apps environment (`availabilityZones` above 1) needs a region
with availability zones.

1354.content: Connect CoreWeave with an API token, prepare the AI Object Storage state bucket, and run container services with GPUs on an existing CKS cluster.

1366.content:
The CoreWeave adapter is covered by unit tests and its OpenTofu modules pass `tofu validate`. It
has not been verified against a live organization yet.

1367.content:
OrkStage creates VPCs and AI Object Storage buckets with the `coreweave/coreweave` OpenTofu
provider. Container services and ingress routes are Kubernetes objects on an **existing**
CoreWeave Kubernetes Service (CKS) cluster, created with the `hashicorp/kubernetes` provider.
OpenTofu state lives in an AI Object Storage bucket you own.

1368.content:
CoreWeave has no managed PostgreSQL, Redis or queue service. Place those resources on another
provider in the same instance; a CoreWeave service that depends on them receives their
connection settings as environment variables and their credentials as a Kubernetes Secret.

1369.content:
| Template resource | Capability      | What gets created                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `network`         | `vpc` (default) | `coreweave_networking_vpc` with pod, service and internal load balancer prefixes ready for a CKS cluster. One zone; internet egress is built in. |

1370.content:
| Template resource           | Capability                 | What gets created                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `compute.container-service` | `cks-deployment` (default) | Namespace, Deployment, Service, optional HorizontalPodAutoscaler and Ingress on the target's cluster |

1371.content:
| Template resource | Capability                    | What gets created                                                                        |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `object-storage`  | `ai-object-storage` (default) | `coreweave_object_storage_bucket`, private, with optional versioning and expiration rule |

1372.content:
| Template resource | Capability              | What gets created                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ingress`         | `cks-ingress` (default) | Host name under the cluster domain, served by the installed controller (CoreWeave Traefik chart) with `cert-manager` TLS |

1373.content: `cpu` and `memoryMiB` become resource requests. Memory is also the limit.

1374.content:
`public: true` creates a `LoadBalancer` Service with the
`service.beta.kubernetes.io/coreweave-load-balancer-type: public` annotation. The module waits
for the public IP and outputs `url`.

1375.content:
`autoscaling` creates a HorizontalPodAutoscaler on CPU. The Deployment then leaves the replica
count to it.

1376.content:
GPUs come from `overrides.coreweave.gpu` in the template. `count` (1 to 8) becomes the
`nvidia.com/gpu` limit; `class` adds required node affinity on the `gpu.nvidia.com/class` node
label. Check the class values on your nodes with `kubectl get nodes -L gpu.nvidia.com/class`.

1377.content:
Each routed service creates an Ingress object for its path in its own namespace, with the ingress
host, the IngressClass and, when `tls` is on, the `cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer` annotation. The
controller merges them under one host. Install the CoreWeave Traefik and `cert-issuer` charts (or set
`ingressClassName`, `clusterIssuer` and `ingressDomain` for your own controller) before deploying.

1378.content:
Connection settings of dependencies (`<ID>_HOST`, `<ID>_PORT`, `<ID>_URL`, `<ID>_BUCKET`,
`<ID>_ENDPOINT`) are plain environment variables. Credentials published through `secret_ref`, for
example a PostgreSQL password on AWS or Supabase, are read from the owning provider at deploy time
and stored in the Kubernetes Secret `<name>-deps`, loaded with `envFrom` as `<ID>_PASSWORD`,
`<ID>_USERNAME`, `<ID>_URL` and so on. They pass to OpenTofu as the sensitive `TF_VAR_secret_env`
and are kept in the OpenTofu state, like any Kubernetes Secret managed by OpenTofu.

1379.content:
| `config` field | Required | Meaning                                                                   |
| -------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `stateBucket`  | yes      | AI Object Storage bucket for OpenTofu state. Must exist before deploying. |

1380.content:
| `config` field | Required                 | Meaning                                         |
| -------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `clusterName`  | for services and ingress | Existing CKS cluster that workloads deploy into |

1381.content:
| `config` field | Required | Meaning                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `zone`         | no       | Zone of the cluster and the state bucket, for example `US-EAST-04A`. Defaults to the deployment region. |

1382.content:
| `config` field  | Required | Meaning                                                    |
| --------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `stateEndpoint` | no       | S3 endpoint for state. Defaults to `https://cwobject.com`. |

1383.content:
| `config` field     | Required | Meaning                                                 |
| ------------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ingressClassName` | no       | IngressClass for ingress routes. Defaults to `traefik`. |

1384.content:
| `config` field  | Required | Meaning                                                                      |
| --------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `clusterIssuer` | no       | `cert-manager` ClusterIssuer for TLS routes. Defaults to `letsencrypt-prod`. |

1385.content:
| `config` field  | Required | Meaning                                                                                                   |
| --------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ingressDomain` | no       | DNS suffix served by the ingress controller. Defaults to `<organization id>-<clusterName>.coreweave.app`. |

1386.content:
`token`: a CoreWeave API access token (Console, Tokens). The OpenTofu runner receives it as
`COREWEAVE_API_TOKEN`. CKS managed auth accepts the same token as a Kubernetes bearer token, so
with `clusterName` set no kubeconfig is needed: the adapter looks up the cluster's API server
endpoint through the CKS API.

1387.content:
`stateAccessKeyId` and `stateSecretAccessKey`: an AI Object Storage access key that can read and
write the state bucket and the buckets OrkStage creates.

1388.content:
`kubeconfig`: only for clusters reached another way (a private endpoint, a different token).
The current context's server, `certificate-authority-data` and bearer `token` are used. Client
certificates and exec plugins are not supported.

1389.content:
Cluster access reaches OpenTofu as `TF_VAR_k8s_host`, `TF_VAR_k8s_token` and `TF_VAR_k8s_ca` for
one command. Nothing is written to disk and no secret is part of the configuration.

1390.content:
AI Object Storage is S3 compatible and accepts only virtual hosted style requests
(`https://<bucket>.cwobject.com`). Before the first deployment:

1391.content:
As an organization admin, create an organization access policy that lets the principal behind
the access key use AI Object Storage (Console, Object Storage, Policies). Without a policy every
S3 request is denied.

1392.content: Create an access key (Console, Object Storage, Keys) and put it in the credential secret.

1394.content:
The S3 backend runs without native locking, because conditional writes are not confirmed for AI
Object Storage. OrkStage already runs one operation per resource at a time.

1395.content:
API token: read the caller identity, list CKS clusters, create and delete VPCs, create and
delete AI Object Storage buckets and their versioning and lifecycle settings.

1397.content:
AI Object Storage access key: read and write the state bucket; read the buckets OrkStage creates
(health checks).

1398.content:
`allowedRegions` and `defaultRegion` are CoreWeave zone names such as `US-EAST-04A`. VPCs and
buckets are created in the deployment region. A VPC lives in one zone.

1399.content:
| Capability       | Action    | Parameters | Effect                                                                                                              |
| ---------------- | --------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cks-deployment` | `restart` | none       | Rolling restart of every pod of the Deployment, like `kubectl rollout restart`, keeping the same image and settings |

1400.content: Logs are the last lines of up to three pods.

1401.content:
OrkStage does not create CKS clusters or node pools. Workloads go to the cluster in
`clusterName` (or the kubeconfig). The `vpc` capability is not attached to that cluster.

1402.content: Images must be pullable by the cluster nodes. Registry pull secrets are not managed.

1403.content:
AI Object Storage access keys are scoped to a principal, not a bucket, so buckets publish no
`secret_ref` and other providers cannot be handed credentials for them.

1404.content:
Buckets have no force destroy: empty a bucket before deleting it. The template `tier` and
`publicAccess` are not applied.

1405.content:
Several routed services request their own certificate for the same host (one per namespace).
Mind the Let's Encrypt duplicate certificate limit.

1406.content: GPU hours are billed per node and are not part of the cost estimate.

1408.content: Connect a DigitalOcean team with an API token and Spaces keys, prepare the state bucket, and see what OrkStage creates on App Platform and managed databases.

1417.content:
The DigitalOcean adapter is covered by unit tests and its OpenTofu modules pass `tofu validate`.
It has not been verified against a live team yet.

1418.content:
OrkStage creates DigitalOcean resources with the OpenTofu modules in
`orkstage-modules/modules/digitalocean`, one isolated state per resource, kept in a Spaces bucket
of your own team. Health, logs, deployments and actions use the DigitalOcean REST API.

1419.content: One cloud target is one DigitalOcean team.

1420.content:
| Template resource | Capability      | What gets created                        |
| ----------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `network`         | `vpc` (default) | VPC. DigitalOcean picks a free IP range. |

1421.content:
| Template resource           | Capability               | What gets created                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `compute.container-service` | `app-platform` (default) | App Platform app with one service component from an image. Size from `cpu` and `memoryMiB`, CPU autoscaling on dedicated sizes, health check, encrypted database URLs. |

1422.content:
| Template resource     | Capability                   | What gets created                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `database.postgresql` | `managed-postgres` (default) | Managed PostgreSQL in the VPC. Trusted sources are limited to the VPC range unless `publicAccess`. HA adds a standby node in the same datacenter. |

1423.content:
| Template resource | Capability                 | What gets created                                                        |
| ----------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `cache.redis`     | `managed-valkey` (default) | Managed Valkey, Redis compatible, TLS, up to two standby nodes, VPC only |

1424.content:
| Template resource | Capability         | What gets created                                                                     |
| ----------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `object-storage`  | `spaces` (default) | Spaces bucket with versioning and expiration lifecycle, private unless `publicAccess` |

1425.content:
| Template resource | Capability                       | What gets created                                                            |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ingress`         | `app-platform-ingress` (default) | No infrastructure: each service applies its route path prefix to its own app |

1426.content:
Database credentials are never module outputs. PostgreSQL and Valkey publish
`secret_ref = do-db://<cluster id>`, and the adapter reads the connection details from the
DigitalOcean API (`readSecret`) when a resource on another provider needs them. App Platform
services receive `<ID>_URL` for each DigitalOcean database they depend on as a `SECRET` variable.

1427.content:
| `config` field | Required | Example                 | Meaning                                   |
| -------------- | -------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `stateBucket`  | yes      | `acme-orkstage-tfstate` | Existing Spaces bucket for OpenTofu state |

1428.content:
| `config` field | Required | Example | Meaning                      |
| -------------- | -------- | ------- | ---------------------------- |
| `stateRegion`  | yes      | `nyc3`  | Spaces region of that bucket |

1429.content:
The values reach OpenTofu only as runner environment variables (`DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN`,
`SPACES_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `SPACES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, and `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and
`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` for the state backend).

1430.content: Create the bucket once, before validating the target. OrkStage never creates it.

1431.content:
The backend signs as `us-east-1` against `https://<stateRegion>.digitaloceanspaces.com`, as
DigitalOcean documents, and locks state with `use_lockfile`.

1432.content:
A full access token works. A custom scoped token needs create, read, update and delete on `vpc`,
`app` and `database`, plus `account:read` and `tag:create`. Validation probes the VPC, App
Platform and database scopes and fails when a scope needed by the resources about to be deployed
is missing.

1434.content:
App Platform joins a VPC only from one datacenter per region: `ams3`, `atl1`, `blr1`, `fra1`,
`lon1`, `nyc1`, `sfo3`, `sgp1`, `syd1`, `tor1`. In other regions (for example `nyc3`) a service
cannot reach a private database, and deploying such a pair fails validation. Use one of those
regions or give the database public access. Spaces is not offered in `nyc1`.

1435.content:
| Capability     | Action     | Parameters                             | Effect                                                                   |
| -------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `app-platform` | `redeploy` | `forceBuild` (boolean, default `true`) | New App Platform deployment of the current spec, pulling the image again |

1436.content:
| Capability     | Action    | Parameters | Effect                                                            |
| -------------- | --------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `app-platform` | `restart` | none       | Rolling restart of the service instances without a new deployment |

1437.content: Deployment history and run logs come from the App Platform API.

1438.content:
App Platform pulls images from DigitalOcean Container Registry, Docker Hub and GHCR only.
Private Docker Hub or GHCR images need registry credentials, which are not wired yet.

1439.content: Autoscaling needs a dedicated CPU instance size. Shared sizes run a fixed instance count.

1440.content:
Credentials of dependencies on other providers reach the service as `<ID>_CREDENTIALS_REF`
references, not values.

1441.content: Services do not receive Spaces keys for their buckets, only the bucket name and endpoint.

1442.content: Managed database backups are daily with 7 days of recovery. Retention is not configurable.

1443.content:
From 15 October 2026 (new accounts) and 30 November 2026 (all accounts), new Standard Edition
PostgreSQL clusters cannot add standby nodes or use plans above 4 GiB. Use
`overrides.digitalocean.size` with an Advanced Edition slug when you need them.

1444.content: A VPC spans the datacenter, so availability zones and NAT gateways are not modelled.

1445.content: There is no load balancer capability yet. `ingress` is App Platform routing only.

1446.content:
Production resources keep `force_destroy` off on buckets. DigitalOcean has no deletion protection
flag for database clusters.

1448.content: Connect a Google Cloud project with a service account key, prepare the GCS state bucket, and see what OrkStage creates on Cloud Run, Cloud SQL and Memorystore.

1457.content:
The Google Cloud adapter is covered by unit tests and its OpenTofu modules pass `tofu validate`.
It has not been verified against a live project yet.

1458.content:
OrkStage creates Google Cloud resources with the OpenTofu modules in
`orkstage-modules/modules/gcp`, one isolated state per resource, kept in a GCS bucket you own.
Health, logs, secrets and redeploys go through the Google Cloud REST APIs.

1459.content:
| Template resource | Capability      | What gets created                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `network`         | `vpc` (default) | Custom mode VPC, one regional subnet with private Google access, a private services access range for Cloud SQL and Memorystore, Cloud NAT when `natGateway` is set |

1460.content:
| Template resource           | Capability            | What gets created                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `compute.container-service` | `cloud-run` (default) | Cloud Run v2 service with its own service account. Direct VPC egress into the subnet when a network is in the slot (all traffic through NAT when the network has one). `replicas` or the autoscaling range sets the instance bounds. Public services accept unauthenticated calls; the others accept internal traffic only. |

1461.content:
| Template resource     | Capability                     | What gets created                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `database.postgresql` | `cloud-sql-postgres` (default) | Cloud SQL Enterprise edition, private IP only when a network is in the slot. Regional availability for `zone-redundant` HA, backups with point in time recovery, deletion protection in production, TLS required. |

1462.content:
| Template resource | Capability                    | What gets created                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cache.redis`     | `memorystore-redis` (default) | Memorystore for Redis: Basic tier without replicas, Standard tier with one replica, read replicas from two. AUTH on. |

1463.content:
| Template resource | Capability      | What gets created                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `object-storage`  | `gcs` (default) | Bucket with uniform access, public access prevention unless `publicAccess`, versioning, class change after 30 days for `infrequent` (Nearline) and `archive`, expiry from `retentionDays` |

1464.content:
| Template resource | Capability                    | What gets created                                                                     |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ingress`         | `cloud-run-ingress` (default) | Nothing: each routed service uses the HTTPS URL Cloud Run gives it and becomes public |

1465.content:
Cloud Run services mount database and cache credentials from Secret Manager as
`<ID>_CREDENTIALS`, and get read and write access to the buckets they depend on.

1466.content:
The PostgreSQL app password lives in OpenTofu state and in a Secret Manager secret
(`secret_ref`). The Redis AUTH string is stored in Secret Manager too. `readSecret` returns
`username`, `password`, `host`, `port`, `database` and `url` for PostgreSQL, and `password`,

1497.content: The clouds and platforms OrkStage deploys to, what each one offers for every resource type, how credentials work and where OpenTofu state lives.

1505.content:
A template names resource types such as `database.postgresql` or `web.frontend`, never a provider.
When you create an instance, each placement slot is bound to a **cloud target** (one account,
project, team or workspace of a provider) and a region. The provider adapter behind that target
turns each resource into real infrastructure.

1506.content:
AWS is tested against MiniStack and runs on real accounts. The other adapters on this page are in
Preview: they are covered by unit tests, and the OpenTofu modules of the
infrastructure clouds pass `tofu validate`, but none of them has been verified against a live
account yet. Expect changes. Preview providers are **disabled by default**; see
enabling a provider.

1507.content:
**Infrastructure clouds** (AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure,
DigitalOcean, Vultr, CoreWeave and Magalu Cloud) are deployed with **OpenTofu**. For each resource,
the worker runs an OpenTofu module in a throwaway runner container. Every resource has its own
state file, kept in a bucket or container **in your own account**. OrkStage keeps outputs and
references, not the state.

1508.content:
**Application platforms** (Vercel, Render and Supabase) are driven through their **REST APIs**.
There is no OpenTofu, no module and no state store: the platform itself holds the state, and the
adapter finds its resources again by name, so repeating a deployment converges the existing
resource instead of creating a second one.

1509.content: Both kinds can be mixed in one instance. See mixing providers.

1510.content:
Each cell is the capability id you can set in a resource's `implementation` field. When a type has
more than one capability, the first one is the default. "Not offered" means the provider has no
capability for that type: place that resource on another provider.

AWS also covers `container-registry` (`ecr`), `queue` (`sqs`) and `dns` (`route53`). No other

1523.content:
Each provider page lists what every capability creates, the settings it ignores and its known
limits. The plan shows the capability chosen for each resource before anything is deployed.

1524.content:
Each provider has a feature flag, `PROVIDER_<NAME>` (for example `PROVIDER_AZURE` or
`PROVIDER_VERCEL`). Only `PROVIDER_AWS` and `PROVIDER_MOCK` (simulation) are on by default. While a
provider's flag is off:

1525.content: registering a target for it fails with `PROVIDER_DISABLED`;

1526.content:
an instance whose placement slot is bound to one of its targets does not compile (create,
update, preview and deploy are refused), and the worker checks again before applying;

1527.content: destroying an instance always works, so turning a provider off never strands resources;

1528.content: simulation targets can still imitate it, which is the way to try a template without an account.

1529.content:
For one tenant, the value comes from the first of these that is set: the tenant's own value, the
platform value, the default. A tenant value therefore wins over the platform value for that
tenant. The same flags also decide what templates may use: `MULTI_CLOUD`, `MULTI_REGION`,
`AUTOSCALING` and `CUSTOM_DOMAINS`, all on by default.

1530.content:
A platform owner changes flags in the console under **Settings > Feature flags**, for the whole
platform or for one tenant, or through the API:

1531.content:
Flag changes need a session with the platform owner role (API keys cannot change them) and are
recorded in the audit log. `GET /cloud/providers` reports whether each provider is enabled.

1532.content:
Platform owners and admins connect accounts in the console with **Cloud targets > Connect a cloud**: a
wizard that turns the provider on if needed, gives the commands that prepare the account, registers the
target and validates it. `ork targets add` does the same from a terminal, and **Register target** is
the short form. The API call underneath is `POST /api/v1/cloud/targets`, with the fields each provider
page lists.

1533.content:
`config` holds only identifiers that are not secret. The API rejects keys that look like secrets
with `422 SECRET_IN_CONFIG`. After registering, click **Validate**: each adapter checks the
configuration, signs in and shows the identity it found. Infrastructure clouds also check that
the state storage answers.

1534.content:
OrkStage never stores provider credentials. A target carries a **`credentialRef`**, a reference to
a secret that the control plane resolves when it needs it:

1535.content:
The secret holds a **JSON object** with the fields the provider page lists, for example
`{ "clientSecret": "<client secret>" }` for Azure. When a provider needs a single field (an API
token or key), the secret can also be the bare value.

1536.content:
Credentials stay in memory. For infrastructure clouds they reach OpenTofu only as environment
variables of one runner command; for application platforms they are sent only to the provider's
API. They are not written to the configuration, the state keys, the database or the logs. See
secret references for the schemes and how they resolve.

The Magalu Cloud adapter is covered by unit tests and its OpenTofu modules pass `tofu validate`.
It has not been verified against a live tenant yet.

1572.content:
OrkStage creates Magalu Cloud resources with the
MagaluCloud/mgc OpenTofu provider
(pinned to `~> 0.56.0`), one isolated state per resource, kept in an Object Storage bucket in your
own tenant. Health, existence checks and restarts use the regional REST API
(`https://api.magalu.cloud/<region>/`, header `X-API-Key`).

1573.content:
| Template resource | Capability      | What gets created                                                |
| ----------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `network`         | `vpc` (default) | VPC, subnet pool, one IPv4 subnet and an internal security group |

| --------------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `compute.container-service` | `vm-docker` (default) | One VM per replica, with Docker installed and started by cloud init. The machine type is the smallest Balanced Value type that fits `cpu` and `memoryMiB`. Public services with more than one replica get a network load balancer on port 80. |

| Template resource     | Capability                 | What gets created                                                                                                         |
| --------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `database.postgresql` | `dbaas-postgres` (default) | DBaaS instance, or a Multi AZ cluster for `zone-redundant`. Private address only. `secret_ref` is `mgc-db://<name>/<id>`. |

| Template resource | Capability                 | What gets created                       |
| ----------------- | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `object-storage`  | `object-storage` (default) | Private bucket with optional versioning |

1577.content:
There is no capability for `cache.redis` or `ingress`. Magalu Cloud has no managed Redis in the
provider. The network load balancer needs its targets at creation time, while OrkStage creates an
ingress before the services it routes to, so load balancing is built into `vm-docker` instead.

1578.content:
DBaaS does not return the master password, so when a resource on another provider needs the
database credentials, the adapter reads the password generated in that database's OpenTofu state
(in your bucket). Inside Magalu Cloud VMs, services receive the reference as
`<ID>_CREDENTIALS_REF`, not the value.

1579.content:
| `config` field | Required | Meaning                                                               |
| -------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `stateBucket`  | yes      | Object Storage bucket for OpenTofu state, in the region you deploy to |

1580.content:

| -------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `sshKeyName`   | no       | Existing SSH key for service VMs. Without it, each service gets its own generated key; the private key stays in state and is never output. |

1581.content:
| Field    | What it is                                                                                               |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apiKey` | API key created in ID Magalu (`id.magalu.com/api-keys`). Used by the OpenTofu provider and the REST API. |

1582.content:
| Field              | What it is                                                          |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `stateAccessKeyId` | Object Storage key pair id of an API key with Object Storage access |

1583.content:
| Field                  | What it is                                     |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `stateSecretAccessKey` | Object Storage key pair secret of the same key |

1584.content:
The key pair reads and writes OpenTofu state and is also given to the provider for bucket
operations. Secrets reach OpenTofu only as runner environment variables: `TF_VAR_mgc_api_key`,
`TF_VAR_mgc_key_pair_id` and `TF_VAR_mgc_key_pair_secret` (sensitive root variables, because the
provider takes these values from configuration only), plus `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and
`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` for the S3 backend.

1585.content:
When creating the API key, grant read and write access to Network (VPC), Virtual Machines, SSH
Keys, DBaaS, Load Balancer and Object Storage. A target that deploys only some resource types can
leave the others out.

1586.content: Create the bucket before validating the target. OrkStage never creates it.

1587.content:
Create it in the target region, keep it private and turn on versioning in the console. State is
reached at `https://<region>.magaluobjects.com` with path style addressing. S3 lock files are off:
Magalu Object Storage support for conditional writes is not documented, and OrkStage already runs
one operation per resource at a time.

1589.content:
| Capability  | Action    | Parameters | Effect                                       |
| ----------- | --------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `vm-docker` | `restart` | none       | Reboots every virtual machine of the service |

1590.content:
The network load balancer is TCP only (no path routing, no TLS termination) and is marked
experimental by Magalu Cloud.

1591.content:
No autoscaling: `replicas` is a fixed VM count. Changing the image or environment replaces the
VMs.

1592.content: Images must be pullable without registry credentials.

1593.content: Environment values are written to VM user data.

1594.content:
VMs get a public IPv4 each so they can pull images. Inbound traffic is limited to the service
port (from anywhere for public services, from the VPC otherwise). `natGateway` is not applied,
and `availabilityZones` does not create more subnets.

1596.content:
Object Storage: `publicAccess`, `tier` and `retentionDays` are not applied, and a bucket must be
empty before it is destroyed.

1597.content:
Magalu Cloud tags are tenant wide and authoritative per resource, so template tags are not
applied.

1598.content: Running containers on Magalu Cloud Kubernetes is not supported.

1600.content: One instance across Vercel, Supabase and AWS S3. Placement slots, how credentials pass between providers, the variables the frontend gets, and triggers.

1610.content:
Each placement slot of a template can go to a different provider, so you can put every part of an
app where it costs least. This page follows the built in **Web app on managed platforms** template
(`web-platforms`) with a common low cost layout:

1614.content:
The Vercel and Supabase adapters are in Preview: covered by unit tests, not yet
verified against live accounts.

1615.content:
`accessKeys: true` on `files` matters here: a Vercel app cannot assume an AWS role, so the AWS
module creates an access key limited to this one bucket for it.

1616.content:
Register one cloud target per provider: a Vercel team, a
Supabase organization and an AWS
account. Each has its own `credentialRef`.

1617.content: Bind each slot to a target and a region, keeping them close to each other:

1618.content:
| Slot  | Target | Region | Resource                |
| ----- | ------ | ------ | ----------------------- |
| `web` | Vercel | `gru1` | `web`, a Vercel project |

1619.content:
| Slot   | Target   | Region      | Resource                       |
| ------ | -------- | ----------- | ------------------------------ |
| `data` | Supabase | `sa-east-1` | `database`, a Supabase project |

1620.content:
| Slot    | Target | Region      | Resource              |
| ------- | ------ | ----------- | --------------------- |
| `files` | AWS    | `sa-east-1` | `files`, an S3 bucket |

1621.content: The Vercel region sets where its functions run, so put it next to the database.

1622.content:
The plan shows the capability chosen for each resource (`vercel-project`, `supabase-postgres`,
`s3`), the cost estimate and the connectivity strategy. `web` and `database` are on different
providers, and the template asks for `mode: secure`, so the plan picks `public-tls`: TLS over the
public network. Supabase connection strings carry `sslmode=require`. See
plan and cost.

1623.content:
The deployment follows the dependency graph: `database` and `files` first, then `web`, which
depends on both.

1624.content:
The frontend needs the database password and the bucket key, but those belong to other providers.
OrkStage moves them at deploy time without keeping a copy:

1625.content: `database` and `files` publish only a reference in their outputs (`secret_ref`), never a value.

1626.content:
When the Vercel adapter deploys `web`, it asks OrkStage for the credentials of each dependency
that has a `secret_ref`.

1627.content:
OrkStage calls `readSecret` on the adapter that **owns** the dependency, with that target's own
credentials:

1628.content:
**Supabase** derives the database password again from the OrkStage encryption key. It is never
stored anywhere: it was derived the same way when the project was created.

1629.content:
**AWS** reads the bucket key from the Secrets Manager secret the module created in your
account, using the deployment role.

1630.content:
The Vercel adapter writes the values to the project as `sensitive` environment variables, which
Vercel never shows again.

1631.content:
The values pass through the control plane's memory only. They are not written to the OrkStage database,
outputs or logs. The S3 key itself lives in your AWS account: in the OpenTofu state in your state
bucket and in the Secrets Manager secret. Its IAM policy allows `s3:ListBucket`,
`s3:GetBucketLocation`, `s3:GetObject`, `s3:PutObject`, `s3:DeleteObject` and
`s3:AbortMultipartUpload` on that bucket only.

1632.content:
Variable names come from the resource id: `database` becomes `DATABASE`, `files` becomes `FILES`
(upper case, any other character turned into `_`). Connection settings from outputs are added as
`<ID>_HOST`, `<ID>_PORT`, `<ID>_URL`, `<ID>_BUCKET`, `<ID>_ENDPOINT` and `<ID>_REGION`. Each
credential field becomes `<ID>_<FIELD>`, with camel case turned into upper snake case
(`poolerUrl` becomes `POOLER_URL`, `secretAccessKey` becomes `SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`). When a name
comes from both, the credential wins and the variable is stored as sensitive.

| Variable               | Value                                   | Vercel type |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME` | `Acme`, from the template `environment` | encrypted   |

1634.content:

| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | Direct connection string with the password, `sslmode=require` | sensitive   |

| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- |
| `DATABASE_POOLER_URL` | Supavisor pooler connection string, when Supabase reports a pooler | sensitive   |

1639.content:

| ------------------- | -------------------- | ----------- |
| `DATABASE_PASSWORD` | The derived password | sensitive   |

1641.content:
| Variable          | Value                                    | Vercel type |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `DATABASE_REGION` | Supabase region, for example `sa-east-1` | encrypted   |

1642.content:
| Variable       | Value       | Vercel type |
| -------------- | ----------- | ----------- |
| `FILES_BUCKET` | Bucket name | sensitive   |

1643.content:
| Variable       | Value                    | Vercel type |
| -------------- | ------------------------ | ----------- |
| `FILES_REGION` | AWS region of the bucket | sensitive   |

1644.content:
| Variable         | Value                                 | Vercel type |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `FILES_ENDPOINT` | Regional HTTPS endpoint of the bucket | encrypted   |

1645.content:
| Variable              | Value                               | Vercel type |

1647.content: The variables are set for the production and preview environments of the project.

1648.content:
Vercel functions connect over IPv4, and the Supabase direct host is IPv6 only unless the project
has the paid IPv4 address option. Use `DATABASE_POOLER_URL` from the app.

1649.content:

1672.content:
The OCI adapter is covered by unit tests and its OpenTofu modules pass `tofu validate`. It has
not been verified against a live tenancy yet.

1673.content:
OrkStage creates OCI resources with the OpenTofu modules in `orkstage-modules/modules/oci`, one
isolated state per resource, kept in an Object Storage bucket of your tenancy through the S3
compatibility API. Identity, health, secrets and actions use the OCI REST APIs with signed
requests (OCI HTTP Signature, `rsa-sha256`).

1674.content: One cloud target is one compartment in one tenancy.
