2403.content:
**Tenant members** see their tenant: every instance with its status, last deployment and estimated
monthly cost, its components with **uptime over the last 30 days** (one bar per day), the open
incidents and the recent activity. With several tenants, a selector switches between them.

2404.content:
Uptime comes from the health checks of the last 30 days. A check counts as up when the resource
was healthy or degraded, and as down when it was unhealthy. Unknown results and planned
maintenance do not count either way. The same data is available at
`GET /tenants/<tenantId>/overview`.

2405.content:
**Platform staff** see instance and deployment counts, health, open incidents and trends across
all tenants. On a new installation the overview also shows an **onboarding checklist**:

2406.content: Connect or validate a cloud target.

2411.content:
The instance list shows the status, health, environment, template version and tenant of each
instance. An instance page has these tabs:

2412.content:
| Tab      | What it shows                                                                                |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Overview | Details, variables, the topology diagram, resources with their placement, outputs and health |

2413.content:
| Tab         | What it shows                                                                           |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plan & cost | A fresh preview: resolved resources, policies, connectivity, cost estimate and the diff |

2414.content:
| Tab         | What it shows                                               |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Deployments | Every deployment of this instance, with status and duration |

2415.content:
| Tab      | What it shows                                           |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Triggers | Provider actions you can run on the instance (triggers) |

2416.content:
| Tab     | What it shows                                  |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Domains | The platform subdomain and your custom domains |

2417.content:
| Tab  | What it shows                                                               |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Logs | Recent log lines per resource (CloudWatch Logs on AWS, simulated elsewhere) |

2418.content:
| Tab     | What it shows                                          |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Metrics | CPU, memory, requests, latency and errors per resource |

2419.content:
The page header holds three actions: **Deploy**, **Upgrade template** and **Destroy**. Each one
appears only when your role allows it.

2420.content:
**Deployments** lists every deployment across the instances you can see. A deployment page shows
the step list, a Gantt timeline, the plan and the event log. When they apply, it also shows
**Approve**, **Cancel** and **Retry**.

2421.content: **Incidents** lists open and resolved incidents with their updates.

2422.content:
The console uses the dark theme by default. Switch to the light theme from the user menu. The
console applies your choice before the first paint, so the page never flashes the wrong theme.

2424.content: Create an OrkStage instance with the six step wizard. Pick the tenant and template, bind each slot to a target and region, then set variables.

2433.content: Doing the same through the API

2434.content:
A new instance starts as a `DRAFT`, and nothing is provisioned until you
deploy it. Open **Instances**, then **New instance**. Creating an
instance needs a platform owner or admin role, or the customer owner or admin role in the tenant.

2435.content:
Choose the customer that owns the instance. The tenant's limits
and feature flags decide what fits, and the instance's cost is attributed to that tenant.

2436.content:
Pick a template and one of its **published** versions. Published versions never change; drafts and
deprecated versions cannot be used. Templates marked `nonProduction` show a warning. The `non-production-template`
policy fails if you use one for a `production` instance.

2437.content:
| Predefined template | Tags                  | Notes              |
| ------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------ |
| `free-validation`   | `sandbox`, `low cost` | Not for production |

2438.content:
| Predefined template | Tags      | Notes              |
| ------------------- | --------- | ------------------ |
| `sandbox-min-cost`  | `sandbox` | Not for production |

2444.content:
| Predefined template | Tags                              | Notes                                             |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `portable-starter`  | `sandbox`, `low cost`, `portable` | Every infrastructure provider; not for production |

2445.content: The size tag (`starter`, `growth`, `scale`) gives an idea of the resources a template needs.

2446.content:
Bind every **placement slot** of the template to a **cloud target** and a **region**. Slots can
use different clouds. With `multicloud-reference`, for example, `primary` can run on AWS, `data` on
Azure and `storage` on OCI. The list offers only targets whose provider the slot accepts, and only
the regions each target allows.

2447.content:
A profile fills every slot at once with the account
and region it names for each provider; you can still change each slot. Tenant members, who do not
see cloud targets, place the instance by choosing a profile.

2448.content:
Simulated targets (the mock provider) carry a simulated label. Use them to rehearse a topology
before you connect real accounts.

2449.content:
Templates expose a few typed variables, for example `apiReplicas` or `databaseSize`. The form
starts with the default values. When every variable has a default, they stay under **Advanced
settings**, closed, because the defaults fit most instances. The browser checks ranges and allowed
values, and the API checks them again.

2450.content:
Give the instance a name and a slug. The slug is lowercase and goes into physical resource names
such as `ork-acme-staging-api`. Then choose the environment: `production`, `staging`, `development`
or `sandbox`. Production instances get stricter policies (backups are required) and an approval
step for high risk changes.

2451.content:
Before anything exists, OrkStage compiles the instance and shows its plan: the resources it would
create on each provider, the policy results, the links between clouds and the estimated monthly
cost. Nothing is saved and no cloud is called (`POST /instances/preview`, with the same body as
`POST /instances`). Issues that make the configuration impossible stop the wizard here. Policy
failures do not stop the creation, but they block deployments until they are fixed.

2452.content:
Check the summary, with the estimated cost, and create the instance. The console opens the
instance page, where the Plan & cost tab previews what a
deployment would do.

2453.content: The API key needs the `instances:write` scope. See API keys.

2455.content: Serve an instance on your own hostname. Prove you own it with a TXT record, point it at the platform, and let OrkStage watch its TLS certificate.

2463.content:
Every instance with a `dns` resource gets a **platform subdomain** in the zone of its cloud target,
for example `production-acme.apps.example.com`, with a managed certificate. You can also serve it
on hostnames you own, such as `api.acme.com`.

2464.content: A custom domain attaches to a resource that can serve one:

2465.content: a `dns` resource whose `customDomain` is `optional` or `required` (it is `disabled` by default);

2466.content: a `web.frontend` resource (Vercel, Render and the other frontend providers).

2467.content:
The tenant also needs the `CUSTOM_DOMAINS` feature, and the `maxDomainsPerInstance` limit, when
set, caps how many custom domains one instance has. The platform subdomain does not count.

2468.content: Open the instance, then the **Domains** tab, and choose **Add domain**.

2469.content: Enter the hostname. When the instance has more than one resource that can serve it, choose one.

2470.content: Create the records the tab shows at your DNS provider:

2471.content:
| Purpose   | Record                               | Value                                             |
| --------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Ownership | `TXT _orkstage-challenge.<hostname>` | The token shown, starting with `orkstage-verify=` |

2472.content:
| Purpose | Record             | Value                                              |
| ------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Routing | `CNAME <hostname>` | The platform subdomain, or the frontend's own host |

2473.content:
| Purpose     | Record                                         | Value                                   |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Certificate | `CNAME` records from the certificate authority | Shown once the certificate is requested |

2474.content:
OrkStage looks up the TXT record about once a minute; **Check now** looks again on the next pass.
When it finds the record, the domain is **Verified** and you get a notification. A domain whose
record does not appear within 7 days is marked **Not verified**; **Check now** gives it another 7
days.

2475.content:
**Deploy** the instance. The deployment attaches the domain to its resource and requests a
certificate for it.

2476.content:
On AWS, the certificate for your hostnames comes from ACM and is validated with the CNAME records
shown under **Certificate**, which you create at your DNS provider, because the zone is yours.
Once ACM issues it, OrkStage tells you, and the next deployment adds it to the HTTPS listener of
the load balancer. Leave the validation records in place: ACM renews the certificate with them.

2477.content:
OrkStage reads the state of each certificate every few minutes: waiting for validation, issued,
expiring soon (30 days or less) or expired. The tenant's owners and admins are notified 30, 14, 7
and 1 day before a certificate expires, once each. A renewed certificate starts the countdown
again.

2478.content:
A hostname belongs to one instance on the whole platform. Adding a hostname that another instance
already has fails with `DOMAIN_TAKEN`, without saying which tenant has it. Hostnames inside the
platform zone are refused. A claim that failed verification does not hold the hostname: someone
who owns it can add it to their own instance.

2479.content:
Removing a custom domain takes it off the list at once. The next deployment detaches it and its
certificate. The platform subdomain goes away with its `dns` resource.

2480.content:
| Request                      | What it does                                       |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /instances/:id/domains` | Domains with their state and the records to create |

2482.content:
| Request                    | What it does                             |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `POST /domains/:id/verify` | Looks up the TXT record on the next pass |

2483.content:
| Request               | What it does            |
| --------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `DELETE /domains/:id` | Removes a custom domain |

2485.content:
Simulated instances use a simulated DNS. The **Create the TXT record (simulation)** button, or
`POST /instances/:id/simulate` with `{ "resourceId": "dns", "domain": { "hostname": "...",
"ownershipRecord": true } }`, creates the ownership record, so the whole flow works without a real
zone. `certificateExpiresAt` in the same object pins when the simulated certificate expires.

2487.content: Start an OrkStage deployment and follow it live. Approve high risk production changes, cancel, retry failed resources, upgrade and destroy safely.

2494.content:
Click **Deploy** on an instance. The API validates the request, records the deployment with all its
steps and answers at once with `202`. The worker then does the work, so you can close the browser.

2495.content:
| Phase                          | What happens                                                                      |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Validate template and policies | The stored snapshot is checked again. A failing policy stops the deployment here. |

2496.content:
| Phase                  | What happens                                                                                           |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Validate cloud targets | Checks credentials, the state bucket and, on real AWS, the IAM permissions the deployed services need. |

2497.content:
| Phase         | What happens                                                                               |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Generate plan | Builds the platform diff, plus a real `tofu plan` for each existing resource that changes. |

2498.content:
| Phase    | What happens                                                                                      |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Approval | Runs only for high risk production changes (see below). Otherwise it is skipped, with the reason. |

2499.content:
| Phase     | What happens                                                                      |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Resources | One step per resource, in dependency order. Independent branches run in parallel. |

2500.content:
| Phase                                      | What happens                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Remove resources no longer in the template | Deletes resources the instance still has but the template no longer contains (after an upgrade, or a resource turned off by a variable), dependents first. The plan lists them as deletions, so production approval covers them. A destroy protected instance keeps them, with a warning. |

2501.content:
| Phase               | What happens                                                                      |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Application rollout | Services run their images by digest, so the exact image never changes under them. |

2502.content:
| Phase                             | What happens                                                         |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Configure secrets and connections | Wires connection references. Secret values stay in the secret store. |

2503.content:
| Phase                                | What happens                                                        |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Health and connectivity verification | Checks each resource until it is healthy, within one settle window. |

2504.content:
| Phase                            | What happens                                                          |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Register observability, Finalize | Registers monitoring and moves the instance to `READY` or `DEGRADED`. |

2505.content:
The deployment page shows each step with its status, the Gantt **timeline** and the **event log**.
It refreshes every 1.5 seconds while the deployment runs.

2506.content:
A deployment of a `production` instance stops at `AWAITING_APPROVAL` when the change is high risk.
That happens in two cases:

2507.content: The platform plan deletes or replaces a resource, or changes an existing database.

2508.content:
The **provider plan** deletes or replaces something. This is a real `tofu plan`, run for each
changed resource during the plan phase. It can find a replacement even when the platform diff
shows only an update, for example when an attribute forces replacement. Routine ECS task
definition revisions do not count.

2509.content:
The event log shows the provider plan for every changed resource, and destructive ones appear as
warnings:

2510.content:
OrkStage notifies the owners and admins, and the `deployment.awaiting_approval` webhook fires. A
user with the `approve` permission clicks **Approve**, and the deployment continues.

2511.content:
When the plan contains no high risk change, the approval step is marked skipped with the reason
`Not needed: no high-risk or destructive changes planned.` Instances in other environments
(`staging`, `development`, `sandbox`) never wait for approval.

2512.content:
Transient failures, such as throttling and timeouts, are retried with exponential backoff.
Destructive operations are never retried automatically.

2513.content:
A failed resource skips only the resources that depend on it, and unrelated branches finish.
Partial failure is a normal outcome, shown per resource. In this example the database fails, so
the API that depends on it is skipped, while storage and the cache finish:

2514.content:
**Retry** runs only the failed and skipped resources again. Resources that already converged are
left alone.

2515.content:
**Cancel** stops the deployment cooperatively. The worker checks for the request while it runs,
and resources that have not started yet are marked cancelled.

2516.content:
If the worker restarts, the deployment resumes. Finished phases are skipped, and converged
resources (same idempotency key) are not applied again.

2517.content:
Someone may delete a resource directly in the provider console. During verification, OrkStage asks
the provider whether each resource still exists. A missing resource fails verification at once,
with the message `Resource no longer exists at the provider. Redeploy to re-create it.`, instead of
waiting for it to settle. The next deployment creates it again.

2518.content:
**Change template version** shows the plan from what runs now to the chosen version (what is
created, updated and deleted), then starts a deployment of that version. The instance keeps its
current version until that deployment succeeds, so a failed upgrade leaves it on the version that
actually runs; **Retry** continues the upgrade. Choosing an older version rolls back the same way.
Production upgrades that delete or replace resources wait for approval. An instance never changes
version on its own.

2519.content:
Through the API: `POST /instances/{id}/preview?templateVersionId={version}` returns the plan, and
`POST /instances/{id}/upgrade` with `{ "templateVersionId": "..." }` starts the deployment.

2520.content: **Destroy** removes every cloud resource in reverse dependency order:

2521.content:
To confirm, you type the instance slug. An instance marked *Destroy protected* refuses to be
destroyed. Only customer owners and admins, and platform owners and admins, can destroy an
instance. Destroying a `production` instance also waits for an approval before anything is
deleted; cancelling it at that point leaves the instance `READY`.

2522.content:
The backup phase checks that a backup policy exists. It does not yet verify that a backup can be
restored.

2524.content: Turn Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes or Docker Compose files into a draft OrkStage template, review the evidence and create the template.

2528.content:
**Templates**, then **Import**, turns existing infrastructure code into a draft template. The
OrkStage scan engine detects and maps the resources. It is the same engine the `ork` CLI uses.

2529.content:
Choose a folder or individual files. The console keeps only the text files the engine understands,
such as `.tf`, `.tf.json`, YAML, JSON, TOML, `Dockerfile`, `package.json`, `go.mod`,
`requirements.txt` and `Chart.yaml`. It skips the `node_modules`, `.git`, `.terraform`, `.next`,
`target`, `vendor`, `dist` and `build` folders. Each file can be at most 512 KiB, and the upload at
most 5 MB in total. The server scans the files with the engine compiled to WebAssembly
(`@orkstage/scan`).

2530.content:
If the server answers `501 SCANNER_UNAVAILABLE`, scanning is not installed on that server. Scan
locally with the CLI instead.

2531.content: `ork import` scans on your machine, sends only the report, and prints a console link:

2532.content: Open the link and the page loads that import directly. The CLI is in Preview.

2533.content: The import page shows five things:

2534.content:
**Resources**: each detected resource with its OrkStage type, provider, implementation,
confidence (`high`, `medium` or `low`) and the source evidence, such as
`main.tf:12 aws_db_instance.main`.

2535.content:
**Connections** inferred from references, for example a task definition that reads the database
address.

2536.content: **Unmapped** items: what the engine saw but cannot express in a template, with the reason.

2537.content: **Warnings** and the **validation** result of the generated template.

2539.content:
Give the template a name and a display name, then click **Create draft and open builder**.
OrkStage creates a `DRAFT` template at version `0.1.0` and opens it in the builder. Fix what the
validation reported, then publish it.

2540.content:
Each import produces at most one template. Only platform owners and admins can create templates.
Other users see a note asking them to share the import id with a platform admin.

2541.content: See Importing IaC for supported sources, mapping rules and the API.

2543.content: Browse curated and community templates with review badges, see their resources and cost before you deploy, and submit your own templates for review.

2550.content:
The marketplace lists templates ready to deploy: complete architectures such as disaster recovery,
a payment gateway, an ecommerce storefront, logistics tracking or last mile delivery. Every
listing is a normal OrkStage template, so it goes through the same placement, plan, policy and
approval checks as any other before anything is created.

2551.content:
| Badge        | Meaning                                                           |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Verified** | Reviewed by platform staff: policies, security defaults and cost. |

2552.content:
| Badge               | Meaning                                                                           |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **DevOps reviewed** | Reviewed for operations: backups, health checks, observability and safe defaults. |

2553.content:
Badges are given by reviewers (platform admins and owners) when they approve a listing. A listing
loses its badges when its author edits it, until it is reviewed again. The curated listings that
ship with OrkStage carry both badges.

2554.content:
Open **Marketplace** in the console. Search by name, summary or tag, and filter by category,
provider or badge; sort by use, date or name. Each card shows the providers the template can run
on, an approximate monthly cost and how often it was starred and used.

2555.content:
A listing page shows the description, every resource with its estimated monthly cost, the
placement slots and the providers each one allows, its tags, its triggers and the full
template source.

2556.content:
The cost is computed on the first provider each placement slot allows, in a representative
region, at static list prices. Your own targets, regions and variables change it. The plan review
before each deployment shows the estimate for your actual choices.

2557.content:
**Use this template** opens the instance wizard with the template and its published version
already selected; you choose the tenant, bind each placement slot to your cloud targets and set
the variables. Templates that need more than one provider need the `MULTI_CLOUD` feature flag,
which is on unless an administrator turned it off.

2558.content:
**Clone and customize** (template authors) copies the template so you can change it in the
builder and publish your own version.

2559.content: **Star** keeps a listing in mind and helps others find popular ones.

2560.content:
Template authors (the `publish` permission on templates) can submit a template that has a
published version: **Marketplace > Submit a template**, then a slug, title, summary, description,
one to four categories and optional tags. The listing stays hidden until it is reviewed; your
submissions and their review notes are under **My submissions**.

2561.content:
Reviewers see the queue under **Review queue** and approve (with badges), reject or later unlist a
listing. Every submission, edit and review is recorded in the audit log.

2562.content:
The same operations are available under `/api/v1/marketplace/listings` (see the
API reference). Browsing and `use` accept API keys with the
`templates:read` scope; submitting and reviewing need a signed in user.

2563.content:
The `TEMPLATE_MARKETPLACE` feature flag (on by default) hides the marketplace for the whole
platform; see enabling a provider for how flags are
changed.

2565.content: Who OrkStage notifies about deployments, incidents, maintenance and domains, through which channels, and how each person chooses what reaches them.

2570.content:
| Channel                                 | How              |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| In the console (the bell in the header) | Always available |

2571.content:
| Channel | How                                                                            |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Email   | SMTP or Amazon SES, through an outbox with retries and a per person rate limit |

2572.content:
| Channel  | How                                               |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Webhooks | HTTP POST of each event as JSON, signed with HMAC |

2573.content:
| Channel | How                                   |
| ------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Slack   | A message to a Slack incoming webhook |

2574.content:
| Channel         | How                                               |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Microsoft Teams | A message to a Teams incoming webhook or workflow |

2575.content:
Slack and Teams are webhook endpoints with another format. Tenant owners and admins add them under
**Integrations**, choose **Send as** Slack message or Microsoft Teams message, paste the incoming
webhook URL and pick the events. The message carries the title, a short text and a link to the
console. The URL must be one of the service's own hosts (`hooks.slack.com` for Slack;
`webhook.office.com`, `logic.azure.com` or `powerplatform.com` for Teams). These messages are not
signed, because Slack and Teams do not check signatures; the retries, the test button and the
automatic disabling after repeated failures work as for other webhooks.

2576.content:
Notifications go to the tenant's **owners and admins** and to **platform owners and admins**.
Examples:

2577.content: a deployment started, succeeded or failed, or a production deployment waits for approval;

2578.content: an instance became degraded, a critical service turned unhealthy, or drift was found;

2579.content: an incident was opened, updated or resolved;

2580.content: maintenance was scheduled, started or completed;

2581.content:
a custom domain was verified or could not be verified, its certificate was issued, or it expires
in 30, 14, 7 or 1 days;

2582.content: someone tried to create an instance beyond the tenant's instance limit.

2583.content:
Each notification in the console links to its deployment, instance, incident or page. Mark it as
read from the bell. The matching API routes are `GET /notifications` and
`POST /notifications/:id/read`.

2584.content:
People who follow a status page get their own emails about incidents and maintenance, see
status pages.

2585.content:
**Notification settings** in the console menu lists every event with two switches: **Console**
and **Email**. Everything is on until you turn it off, and your choices apply to you only. The API
is `GET` and `PUT /me/notification-preferences`:

2586.content:
Slack and Teams messages go to channels of the whole tenant, so they are set per endpoint under
Integrations, not per person.

2587.content: The worker queues emails in an outbox and retries a failed one later, up to 5 attempts in total.

2590.content:
| Variable     | Meaning                                                     |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `EMAIL_FROM` | The sender address; with SES it must be a verified identity |

2591.content:
| Variable                    | Meaning                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `EMAIL_RATE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR` | Emails one person receives per hour at most (default 30); the rest stay in the console |

2592.content:
With `ses`, the worker sends through Amazon SES v2 with its own AWS credentials and `AWS_REGION`,
never with the role of a cloud target. In the local stack, emails land in Mailpit at
http://localhost:8025.

2594.content: Inspect a running OrkStage instance. The topology diagram with placement and health, drift, resource outputs, recent logs and metrics per resource.

2601.content:
The **Overview** tab of an instance draws its topology. Every resource is a node, grouped by
provider, target and region. Dependency edges connect the nodes, and connectivity links carry the
strategy label, for example `public-tls-allowlist` between AWS and Azure. Node colors follow
health, and simulated resources carry a *simulated* label.

2602.content:
**Copy as Mermaid** copies the same diagram as a Mermaid flowchart, ready for a design document or
a pull request description.

2603.content:
Below the diagram, the resource table shows each resource's type, capability, physical name, target
and region, knowledge state (`DESIRED`, `KNOWN`, `ACTUAL` or `UNKNOWN`), drift and health.

2604.content:
On real providers, the worker runs a scheduled **drift scan**. It runs every
`DRIFT_CHECK_INTERVAL_MINUTES` minutes (default 360), and `0` turns it off. The scan plans each
applied resource again with OpenTofu, from the snapshot it was deployed with. If that plan contains
any change, something changed outside OrkStage.

2605.content:
When that happens, OrkStage marks the resource `DRIFT_DETECTED` with the planned actions, writes an
audit event and notifies owners and admins (`instance.drift_detected`). Resources with a pending
change are skipped, because that change is a deployment, not drift. **Deploy** restores the
template's configuration.

2606.content: On simulated targets, drift is checked on every health check instead.

2607.content:
Each provisioned resource exposes the outputs its module produced, for example the database `host`
and `port`, the ingress `url`, the queue `queue_url` or the bucket `endpoint`. Secrets are never
outputs. The database password lives in AWS Secrets Manager, and services receive its ARN.

2608.content:
The **Logs** tab shows recent log lines for a resource
(`GET /instances/:id/logs?resourceId=&limit=`). On AWS they come from the service's CloudWatch log
group. On simulated targets they are generated.

2609.content:
The **Metrics** tab charts CPU, memory, requests per minute, p95 latency and errors per minute for
the last hour (`GET /instances/:id/metrics?resourceId=&metric=cpu&minutes=60`).

2610.content:
On AWS the points come from CloudWatch (`GetMetricData`, one point per minute) for ECS services,
load balancers, RDS databases and ElastiCache clusters. The deployment role already grants
`cloudwatch:GetMetricData`. On simulated targets the points are generated. Other providers show no
metrics yet.

2611.content:
To be told when a metric crosses a threshold, add a metric rule on the
Alert rules page.

2612.content:
On simulated targets, users who can deploy or update the instance see **Simulation controls**:
**Mark unhealthy**, **Mark degraded**, **Mark healthy**, **Clear health override** and **Introduce
drift** (or **Clear drift**). They drive the loop from health to incident to notification without
breaking anything real.

2614.content: Read an OrkStage plan before you deploy. Placement per provider, policy results, connectivity across clouds, monthly cost, the diff and its risk.

2620.content: What OrkStage wires for a link between clouds

2623.content:
The **Plan & cost** tab of an instance runs a preview (`POST /instances/:id/preview`). The preview
compiles the template with the instance's variables and placements, then compares the result with
what OrkStage already knows about the instance. It never touches a cloud and saves nothing.

2624.content:
The preview lists every resource with the target, region and concrete capability it resolved to,
for example `database → Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server (eastus)`. When a capability
is not available in a region, the preview fails and suggests alternatives.

2625.content: Every policy reports a result, so you see everything that was checked, not only what failed:

2626.content:
| Policy               | Checks                                |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `no-public-database` | No database has `publicAccess: true`. |

2627.content:
| Policy              | Checks                               |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `no-public-storage` | Object storage blocks public access. |

2628.content:
| Policy               | Checks                                     |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `production-backups` | Production databases have backups enabled. |

2629.content:
| Policy                    | Checks                                                                               |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `non-production-template` | Sandbox templates are not used for production. For other environments it only warns. |

2630.content:
| Policy                | Checks                                               |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `encryption-required` | Every chosen capability supports encryption at rest. |

2631.content:
| Policy            | Checks                                              |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `allowed-regions` | The target and the platform both allow each region. |

2632.content:
| Policy         | Checks                                                                |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `max-replicas` | Replica counts stay under the platform limit, when one is configured. |

2633.content:
| Policy             | Checks                                                               |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `max-monthly-cost` | The estimate stays under the monthly budget, when one is configured. |

2634.content:
| Policy                | Checks                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `multi-cloud-allowed` | The `MULTI_CLOUD` and `MULTI_REGION` feature flags allow several clouds, or several regions of one provider, when the placements use them. |

2635.content:
| Policy                     | Checks                                                                 |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cross-cloud-connectivity` | Links between clouds can be satisfied. Warns about latency and egress. |

2636.content:
| Policy                   | Checks                                                                            |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `approved-machine-sizes` | Every service uses an approved size (vCPU and memory), when sizes are configured. |

2637.content:
| Policy                | Checks                                                                                       |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `approved-registries` | Every service image starts with an approved registry prefix, when registries are configured. |

2638.content:
| Policy            | Checks                                     |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `required-labels` | The instance carries every required label. |

2639.content:
| Policy        | Checks                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `minimum-tls` | Load balancers accept only the configured TLS version and newer. Enforced on AWS; a warning on providers where OrkStage cannot set it. |

2640.content:
| Policy              | Checks                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mandatory-logging` | Service logs are kept at least the configured number of days. Enforced on AWS (CloudWatch, rounded up to an accepted period); a warning elsewhere. |

2641.content: A `fail` result blocks the deployment. Custom templates go through the same policies.

2642.content: The values behind these policies are data, set on **Policies** in the console or through the API:

2643.content:
**Platform staff** set the platform policy (`GET` and `PUT /policies`). It applies to every
tenant and is the only place where a built in policy can be turned off.

2644.content:
**Tenant owners and admins** set their tenant's policy (`GET` and `PUT /tenants/:id/policy`). It
can only tighten the platform policy: regions, sizes and registries narrow, budgets and replica
limits go down, required labels add up, and the TLS version and log retention go up.

2645.content:
The page also shows the **policy in effect** for the tenant, which is what every preview and
deployment is checked against. API keys cannot change policies.

2646.content:
Labels are key and value pairs on an instance, edited on its Overview tab or sent as `labels` when
it is created or updated. They become tags on every cloud resource of the instance, next to the
platform tags (which win on a clash and whose `platform` prefix is reserved). A policy can require
some of them, for example `team`, so every resource can be traced to its owner and cost center.

2647.content: For each connectivity requirement in the template, the compiler chooses a strategy:

2648.content:
| Strategy          | When                                              |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `private-network` | Both resources are in the same target and region. |

2649.content:
| Strategy          | When                                                                      |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `private-peering` | Same provider, different account or region. Peering cost and setup apply. |

2650.content:
| Strategy     | When                                                                                     |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `public-tls` | The requirement's mode is `secure`: TLS over the provider network or the public network. |

2651.content:
| Strategy               | When                                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `public-tls-allowlist` | Across clouds with `private-preferred`: TLS on a public endpoint that allows only listed sources. |

2652.content:
| Strategy        | When                                                                     |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `unsatisfiable` | Across clouds with `private-required`. Change the mode or the placement. |

2653.content:
OrkStage never creates VPNs or interconnects without telling you. Links between clouds add latency
and may incur egress charges, and the preview says so.

2654.content: The plan shows, for each link between clouds, what OrkStage does besides choosing the strategy:

2655.content:
**Credentials.** When the consumer runs on AWS, Azure or Google Cloud and the database lives on
another provider, OrkStage reads the database credentials from the provider that owns them and
copies them into the consumer's own secret store at deploy time: one Secrets Manager secret on
AWS, Container Apps secrets on Azure, Secret Manager on Google Cloud. The service receives them as
`<ID>_USERNAME`, `<ID>_PASSWORD` and so on. The values pass to OpenTofu as a sensitive variable
and never appear in the stored configuration. On other providers the service receives only the
reference, `<ID>_CREDENTIALS_REF`, and reads it at start.

2656.content:
**Allowlist.** For `public-tls-allowlist`, the database waits for the consumer's network and its
firewall allows only that network's egress addresses: Azure PostgreSQL firewall rules (replacing
the rule that admits every Azure service) or Cloud SQL authorized networks. The network needs a
NAT gateway (`natGateway: true`) for a fixed egress address; the plan says so when it has none.
PostgreSQL on AWS and OCI has no public endpoint, so a consumer on another cloud cannot reach it
without a VPN or interconnect, and the plan says that too.

2658.content:
The estimate uses static list prices from each capability catalog (on demand, monthly, in USD). It
is always labeled **approximate** and is not an invoice. Its confidence is `approximate` when every
resource has a price, `partial` when some do not, and `unavailable` when none do. Lines are grouped
by category: compute, database, cache, storage, network and messaging.

2659.content:
The diff against known resources lists each resource as `CREATE`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE` or `NOOP`,
grouped by provider, target and region. A change of target, region or capability counts as a
replacement. Approval requests and logs use the same plan in plain text:

2660.content:
| Risk   | When                                                              |
| ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `high` | Anything is deleted or replaced, or an existing database changes. |

2661.content:
| Risk     | When                            |
| -------- | ------------------------------- |
| `medium` | Existing resources are updated. |

2662.content:
| Risk  | When                                                 |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `low` | The plan only creates resources, or changes nothing. |

2663.content:
The preview shows the platform's view. During the deployment, the worker also runs the real
provider plan for each resource that changes. See Deploying.

2665.content: The seven predefined OrkStage roles (three for the platform, four per tenant), what each can do, and how every request enforces tenant isolation.

2671.content:
OrkStage has seven predefined roles. **Platform roles** apply to the whole installation. **Tenant
roles** apply per tenant, so one user can be an admin in one tenant and a viewer in another.

2672.content:
| Role            | Can                                    |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `PlatformOwner` | Everything, including global settings. |

2673.content:
| Role            | Can                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `PlatformAdmin` | Everything except changing global settings (it can read them) and deleting the organization. Manages cloud targets, templates and tenants. |

2674.content:
| Role               | Can                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PlatformOperator` | Read everything except settings. Deploy, restart, scale and approve instances. Create and update incidents, and update status pages. Cannot manage cloud targets, publish templates or destroy instances. |

2675.content:
| Capability                                                                   | Owner | Admin | Developer | Viewer |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ----- | --------- | ------ |
| Read instances, deployments, services, incidents, status page, notifications | ✓     | ✓     | ✓         | ✓      |

2676.content:
| Capability                                           | Owner | Admin | Developer | Viewer |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ----- | --------- | ------ |
| Read templates, applications and the tenant's limits | ✓     | ✓     | ✓         | ✓      |

2677.content:
| Capability                   | Owner | Admin | Developer | Viewer |
| ---------------------------- | ----- | ----- | --------- | ------ |
| Deploy and restart instances | ✓     | ✓     | ✓         |        |

2678.content:
| Capability | Owner | Admin | Developer | Viewer |
| ---------- | ----- | ----- | --------- | ------ |
| Import IaC | ✓     | ✓     | ✓         |        |

2679.content:
| Capability                                           | Owner | Admin | Developer | Viewer |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ----- | --------- | ------ |
| Create, update, scale, destroy and approve instances | ✓     | ✓     |           |        |

2680.content:
| Capability                                     | Owner | Admin | Developer | Viewer |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ----- | ----- | --------- | ------ |
| See the team (members and pending invitations) | ✓     | ✓     | ✓         | ✓      |

2681.content:
| Capability         | Owner | Admin | Developer | Viewer |
| ------------------ | ----- | ----- | --------- | ------ |
| Read the audit log | ✓     | ✓     |           |        |

2682.content:
| Capability                   | Owner | Admin | Developer | Viewer |
| ---------------------------- | ----- | ----- | --------- | ------ |
| Manage API keys and webhooks | ✓     | ✓     |           |        |

2683.content:
| Capability                                                     | Owner | Admin | Developer | Viewer |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ----- | --------- | ------ |
| Invite people, change roles, remove members, update the tenant | ✓     |       |           |        |

2684.content: Tenant roles never get access to cloud targets, settings or template publishing.

2685.content:
**Settings > Team** lists the members of a tenant with their roles, and the invitations still
pending. Owners (and platform staff) invite people by email with a role:

2686.content:
The person receives an email with a link that works once and expires after 7 days. The inviter
also sees the link once, to share it directly if the email does not arrive.

2687.content:
They accept it signed in with the invited address; another account is refused. If they sign in
through SSO for the first time with that address, the account is created with the invitation's
membership.

2688.content: Inviting the same address again replaces the previous link. Owners can revoke an invitation.

2689.content:
Owners change roles and remove members; anyone can leave a tenant. A tenant always keeps at least
one owner, so the last owner cannot be demoted or removed until someone else is an owner. Every
invitation, acceptance, role change and removal is in the audit log.

2691.content: The request is authenticated with a session cookie or an API key.

2692.content: Queries for records that belong to a tenant are filtered by the caller's memberships.

2693.content: Every loaded record is checked against the same rules (CASL) before any action.

2694.content: The action is written to the audit log.

2695.content:
A request for another tenant's record gets **404**, not 403, so the response does not reveal that
the record exists. The console receives the rules from `GET /me` only to hide what you cannot do.
The API remains the authority.

2696.content:
An API key acts **with a role**. A tenant key uses `CustomerAdmin`, `CustomerDeveloper` or
`CustomerViewer`. A key for the whole organization uses `PlatformAdmin` or `PlatformOperator`.
Scopes then narrow what the role allows, so a key can never do more than its role.

2697.content:
Custom roles and finer permissions are planned for the Enterprise edition. See
Community vs Enterprise.

2699.content: How OrkStage derives instance health, shows it on a status page per tenant, opens incidents from health checks and metrics, and posts incident updates.

2700.content: From resource health to instance health

2707.content: Trying a metric alert on a simulated target

2710.content:
The worker's health monitor checks every active resource through its provider adapter at a fixed
interval: `HEALTH_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, 30 by default. Instance health then follows from the
health of its components:

2712.content:
| Components                                 | Instance   |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------- |
| Any component is `UNHEALTHY` or `DEGRADED` | `DEGRADED` |

2713.content:
| Components                    | Instance                                    |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Some components are `UNKNOWN` | `DEGRADED` (`UNKNOWN` when all are unknown) |

2714.content:
| Components                          | Instance      |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------- |
| All components are in `MAINTENANCE` | `MAINTENANCE` |

2716.content:
Services and databases are critical by default. Caches, queues and storage are not. A template can
change this per resource with the `critical` field.

2717.content:
Each tenant has a **status page**, at `/status/<tenantId>` in the console. It groups resources into
components that customers see: API, Workers, Database, Cache, Messaging, Storage, and DNS & TLS.
The headline shows the worst component state.

2724.content:
Tenant owners and admins choose under **Settings** on the status page
(`/status/<tenantId>/settings`):

2725.content:
| Visibility             | Who reads the page                                |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Owners and admins only | Platform staff and the tenant's owners and admins |

2726.content:
| Visibility                           | Who reads the page                       |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| Every member of the tenant (default) | Everyone in the tenant, after signing in |

2727.content:
| Visibility           | Who reads the page                                |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Anyone with the link | Also people without an account, at `/s/<address>` |

2728.content:
A **public page** shows the title and description you set, component names and states, incidents
and maintenance. It never shows resource ids, providers, regions or alert details. Incidents that
OrkStage opened on its own read as a plain impact, such as "Degraded performance on Acme
production", and their automatic updates as plain sentences. Incidents and updates written by
people appear as written. Resolved incidents stay listed for 14 days. The public address is
answered with its own rate limits, and an address that is not public looks exactly like one that
does not exist.

2729.content:
The same settings page renames components (for example API to Checkout), hides them or changes
their order. Their status still follows the resources behind them.

2730.content:
Anyone who can read the page can get an email when an incident opens, changes or resolves, and
when maintenance is scheduled, starts and ends:

2731.content: In the console, **Email me updates** on the status page subscribes your own address at once.

2732.content: On a public page, people enter an address and confirm it from the email they receive.

2733.content:
Every email ends with an unsubscribe link. People who subscribed on the public page stop getting
emails while the page is not public. The settings page shows how many confirmed subscribers there
are. Emails go through the SMTP server of the platform (see
configuration).

2734.content: Alert rules decide when OrkStage opens an incident on its own. There are two kinds:

2735.content: **Health rules** count failed health checks in a row.

2736.content:
**Metric rules** compare a statistic of a metric (average, maximum or minimum) over a window of
minutes with a threshold, for example "average CPU % above 80 over 5 minutes".

2738.content:
| Rule                          | Opens an incident after         | Severity | Cooldown   |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------- | -------- | ---------- |
| `Critical resource unhealthy` | 3 failed health checks in a row | high     | 15 minutes |

2739.content:
| Rule                              | Opens an incident after         | Severity | Cooldown   |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | -------- | ---------- |
| `Non-critical resource unhealthy` | 5 failed health checks in a row | medium   | 30 minutes |

2741.content:
They are **deduplicated** per rule and resource. A resource has at most one open incident for a
rule, so a flapping resource never opens many.

2742.content:
After an incident resolves, a **cooldown** passes before a new one can open for the same
resource and rule.

2743.content:
They are **resolved automatically** when health returns or the metric is back within the
threshold, with a final update. A rule with **Resolve when it clears** turned off leaves the
incident open for a person to close.

2744.content:
**Alert rules**, in the console menu (`/settings/alerts`), lists the rules that apply to you and
lets you add, edit, turn off and delete them.

2745.content:
Platform staff manage every rule. A rule without a tenant is a **platform rule** and applies to
every tenant.

2746.content: Tenant owners and admins manage their own tenant's rules. Other members read them.

2747.content: A metric rule has these fields:

2749.content:
| Field     | Meaning                                                                                      |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Resources | Only one resource type, such as `compute.container-service`, or any resource with the metric |

2750.content:
| Field     | Meaning                                                 |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Statistic | average, maximum or minimum of the points in the window |

2752.content:
| Field  | Meaning                               |
| ------ | ------------------------------------- |
| Window | Minutes of data, one point per minute |

2753.content:
| Field              | Meaning             |
| ------------------ | ------------------- |
| Severity, cooldown | As for health rules |

2754.content:
| Field   | Meaning                                    |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Actions | Open an incident; notify the tenant owners |

2755.content:
The worker reads each metric rule at most once a minute per instance, because provider metric APIs
are billed per request. When the provider has no data for the window, the rule waits.

2757.content:
| Provider | Metrics                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| AWS      | CloudWatch `GetMetricData`: ECS service CPU and memory; load balancer requests, 5xx errors and latency; RDS CPU and connections; ElastiCache CPU and connections |

2758.content:
| Provider          | Metrics                                                            |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Simulated targets | A generated series between 20 and 60, which you can pin to a value |

2759.content:
| Provider        | Metrics                                       |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Other providers | None yet. Metric rules have no effect on them |

2760.content:
The same rules are available through the API at `/alert-rules` (`GET`, `POST`, `PATCH`,
`DELETE`). Reading needs the `instances:read` scope and changing needs `incidents:write`.

2761.content: Pin a metric of a resource to a value, wait for the rule to fire, then let it go back:

2762.content:
The incident opens within a minute or two of the pin, depending on the window, and resolves the
same way after you clear it.

2763.content:
Platform staff (owners, admins and operators) can open an incident by hand and post updates. Each
update has a status, a message and an optional impact. Tenant members can read incidents and their
updates, which appear on the incident page in order. Through the API, this needs the
`incidents:write` scope.

2764.content:
Owners, admins and platform staff schedule maintenance under **Settings** on the status page: a
title, a message, when it starts and ends, and which instance and components it covers (all of
them when none are chosen).

2765.content: Before it starts, the status page lists it as scheduled.

2766.content:
While it runs, its components show `MAINTENANCE`, and their resources open no incidents from
health or metric rules.

2767.content:
Subscribers and the tenant's owners and admins are told when it is scheduled, when it starts and
when it ends.

2768.content:
Cancelling a window that has not started deletes it. Ending a running one stops it now and keeps
it in the history.

2769.content:
Through the API: `GET`, `POST` and `PATCH /maintenance-windows`, and `DELETE /maintenance-windows/:id`
to cancel or end one. Changing them needs the `incidents:write` scope.

2771.content: Create, clone, validate and publish OrkStage templates in the console, in the YAML editor or the drag and drop builder that edits the same document.

2776.content:
Platform staff manage templates: owners and admins publish them, and operators can read them.
Tenants use published versions when they create instances.

2777.content: **New template** creates the first version as a draft.

2778.content:
**Edit draft** changes the YAML of a draft. Its name and version stay; to change the version,
add a new one.

2780.content:
**Publish** runs the full validation and refuses unsafe templates. It also refuses a version
when no shared cloud target can host every placement slot, because the capability and policy
checks could not run (`CAPABILITY_UNCHECKED`). Add a target for the providers the slots allow,
or widen the slots, and publish again.

2781.content:
Published and deprecated versions never change. The database refuses any change to their source,
not only the API, because instances record the version they run.

2782.content:
**Deprecate** retires a published version, with an optional note. Instances on it keep running
and can still be deployed; new instances and upgrades are refused with `TEMPLATE_DEPRECATED` and
the note. **Restore** makes it published again.

2783.content: **Compare with** shows the YAML changes between the selected version and any other one.

2784.content: **Clone** copies a template under a new name, for example to start from a predefined one.

2785.content: An instance keeps its version until someone runs **Upgrade template** on it.

2786.content:
The built in templates follow the same rules: when OrkStage ships a newer built in version, the
older one becomes deprecated and its instances keep running.

2787.content: Validation runs in stages and reports every issue with its stage, severity, code and path:

2788.content:
| Stage    | Checks                                                                     |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `schema` | YAML syntax and the `platform/v1` schema (types, ranges, required fields). |

2789.content:
| Stage      | Checks                                                                                                |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `semantic` | Unique ids, valid references (`dependsOn`, routes, DNS target, variables), existing slots, no cycles. |

2790.content:
| Stage    | Checks                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `limits` | Only when a tenant is chosen: the template fits that tenant's limits (services, vCPU, memory, replicas, database storage, custom domains, backup retention) and its feature flags allow autoscaling and custom domains. |

2791.content:
| Stage        | Checks                                                                             |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `capability` | The providers each slot allows can implement every resource. Includes suggestions. |

2792.content:
| Stage    | Checks                                                       |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `policy` | Governance policies that can be checked without an instance. |

2793.content:
CI can run the same validation without storing anything: `POST /templates/validate` (see
CI/CD intake).

2794.content:
To open the builder, choose **Templates**, then **New**, then **Builder**, or click **Builder** on
an existing template. It is a drag and drop canvas:

2795.content: Drag resource types from the palette onto the canvas.

2796.content: Placement slots are lanes. Drop a resource into a lane to place it, and add or remove lanes.

2797.content: Connect nodes to add dependencies and connectivity requirements, with protocol, port and mode.

2798.content: Edit each resource's fields in the side panel, under the same constraints as the schema.

2799.content:
The builder edits **the same YAML document** you see in the source view and validates it as you
work, so you can switch between the two at any time.

2800.content:
The template reference describes the full format. If you
keep templates in a repository, the `ork` CLI pushes them as new versions
(Preview). IaC import can draft a template from existing
Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes or Compose files.

2802.content: Run provider actions on a deployed instance (redeploy, restart, rollback, purge cache, backup) by hand, from CI with an API key, or on a schedule.

2807.content:
Triggers are declared in the template (reference)
and apply to every instance built from it. Each one runs a single action on a single resource
through the provider that owns it, so the action and its parameters depend on the provider: a
Vercel project offers `redeploy`, `promote`, `rollback` and `purge-cache`; a Render service offers
`redeploy`, `restart`, `rollback`, `scale`, `suspend` and `resume`; a Supabase database offers
`restart`, `pause`, `restore` and `backup`; a Cloud Run or Container Apps service offers `redeploy`
or `restart`.

2808.content:
A trigger starts work at the provider and records the result: the provider deployment or backup
it started, a link when there is one, and a message. It does not wait for a build to finish; the
instance health and the provider deployment history show how that ends.

2809.content:
Open the instance and choose **Triggers**. Each trigger shows the resource and action, how it can
run (manual, API key, schedule) and its last result. **Run** opens the parameters the template
marks as overridable; everything else keeps its template value. Running a trigger needs the
deploy permission on the instance.

2810.content:
A trigger is unavailable while its resource is not deployed, or when the provider of that
resource does not offer the action (for example a template that asks for `backup` on a provider
without on demand backups). The console shows the reason.

2811.content:
Triggers with `on.webhook: true` accept calls from an API key with
the `instances:deploy` scope:

2812.content:
The call returns `202` with the run (`status: QUEUED`). Parameters that are not overridable,
unknown to the action or of the wrong type are rejected with `422` before anything reaches the
provider. A trigger without `on.webhook` refuses API keys with `403`.

2813.content:
`on.schedule` takes a five field cron expression in UTC. The worker keeps one schedule per
trigger and instance, replaces it after every deployment (so a changed or removed schedule takes
effect with the next deploy) and removes it when the instance is destroyed. Scheduled runs are
skipped while the instance is not `READY` or `DEGRADED`.

2814.content:
Every run is stored with its source (`MANUAL`, `SCHEDULE`, `WEBHOOK`), parameters, status and
result, and appears under **Recent runs** and in `GET /instances/{id}/trigger-runs`. Runs are
audited, and their outcome is sent as the `trigger.succeeded` and `trigger.failed`
notification and webhook events.

orderedDocs:
"OrkStage" and the OrkStage logo are trademarks of the project. Forks must use a different name and
logo. The trademark policy lists what is fine, what needs permission and what is not
allowed.
[ ] `NODE_ENV=production`, dev login off and an OIDC provider configured.
[ ] `SESSION_SECRET` and `ENCRYPTION_KEY` generated at random and injected from a secret store.
**A budget alert** on the account, before any deployment. Each section says where.

**A clear boundary.** Core code never imports Enterprise code; the platform loads the Enterprise
module only when the build has it, and Enterprise features plug into extension points. Without a license that covers them, gated endpoints answer `402 ENTERPRISE_REQUIRED`.

**A license key turns it on.** Set `ORKSTAGE_LICENSE_KEY` to the key you receive. The key is a
signed token (Ed25519) that OrkStage verifies **offline**. OrkStage does not contact a license
server and does not require usage reports.

**Accepted.** `CloudProviderAdapter` is the only way the platform touches a cloud. Its
`ensureResource` call converges a resource to the desired state, so a retry cannot create a
duplicate.

**Accepted.** All tenants share one database, and every row a tenant owns carries a `tenantId`.
Isolation works in four layers: the request principal, query scoping by membership, a CASL check
on the loaded record, and the audit log. A record from another tenant is reported as not found.

**Accepted.** Every `tofu` command runs in a throwaway container with a pinned image. Credentials
exist only in that container's environment.

**Accepted.** Templates are shared across tenants, but each tenant has its own cloud accounts. So
the provider, account and region cannot live in the template.

**Accepted.** Temporal would add a cluster to operate. BullMQ reuses the Redis and Postgres that
the platform already requires.

**Alert rules**, in the console menu (`/settings/alerts`), lists the rules that apply to you and
lets you add, edit, turn off and delete them.

**Allowlist.** For `public-tls-allowlist`, the database waits for the consumer's network and its
firewall allows only that network's egress addresses: Azure PostgreSQL firewall rules (replacing
the rule that admits every Azure service) or Cloud SQL authorized networks. The network needs a
NAT gateway (`natGateway: true`) for a fixed egress address; the plan says so when it has none.
PostgreSQL on AWS and OCI has no public endpoint, so a consumer on another cloud cannot reach it
without a VPN or interconnect, and the plan says that too.

**An AWS CLI profile** on the development stack: `AWS_PROFILE=<name> pnpm platform:aws-real` in the

`CloudProviderAdapter` is the only way the platform touches a cloud. It defines `validateTarget`,
`capabilities`, an idempotent `ensureResource`, `deleteResource`, `getResource` and `checkHealth`, plus
optional logs, metrics, plan and existence probes. One shared contract test suite runs against every
adapter.

`config` holds only identifiers that are not secret. The API rejects keys that look like secrets
with `422 SECRET_IN_CONFIG`. After registering, click **Validate**: each adapter checks the
configuration, signs in and shows the identity it found. Infrastructure clouds also check that
the state storage answers.

`config` must not contain secrets. The API rejects keys that look like secrets with
`422 SECRET_IN_CONFIG`, and a role from another account than `accountId` with `422 INVALID_CONFIG`. `credentialRef` must be an `env://` or `aws-sm://` reference, and any other
value is rejected. You can assign a target to one tenant (`tenantId`) or share it across tenants.
`cpu` and `memoryMiB` become resource requests. Memory is also the limit.
`database` and `files` publish only a reference in their outputs (`secret_ref`), never a value.
`digest` must be `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex characters.

trigger and instance, replaces it after every deployment (so a changed or removed schedule takes
effect with the next deploy) and removes it when the instance is destroyed. Scheduled runs are
skipped while the instance is not `READY` or `DEGRADED`.

`ork` turns an existing project into an OrkStage template, pushes it, and deploys and operates
instances from your terminal or from CI. It reads Terraform and OpenTofu, CloudFormation, SAM and
CDK, Kubernetes and Helm, Docker Compose, Dockerfiles and package manifests. It also detects Pulumi,

TypeScript 7 with `module: NodeNext`.

endpoint through the CKS API.

| Area     | Control                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Webhooks | HMAC-SHA256 signatures with a timestamp, and `https` only. SSRF protection blocks private, loopback, link local and multicast targets, checked at registration and again before each delivery. No redirects are followed, the timeout is 10 seconds, and signing secrets are encrypted at rest. |

| Area     | Control                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| API keys | Only the SHA-256 hash of the token is stored. Scopes narrow a role and never exceed it. A key cannot manage keys. Keys support expiry, revocation and a last used time. Every action is audited with the key's name and prefix. |

| Area     | Control                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sessions | An opaque random token of 32 bytes in an `httpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` cookie (`Secure` in production). Only its SHA-256 hash is stored. Sessions expire after 12 hours and are revoked on logout. |

| Area    | Community (AGPL-3.0)           | Enterprise                                                                     |
| ------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Support | Community (GitHub Discussions) | Support backed by an SLA, security advisories before public disclosure planned |

| Area    | Control                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Secrets | The API rejects target configuration with keys that look like secrets. Credentials are `env://` or `aws-sm://` references. Services receive secret references, not values. |

| Area    | Control                                                                                                                          |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Logging | Pino redacts tokens, secrets, cookies and authorization headers. Errors return a code and a correlation id, never a stack trace. |

| Area    | Control                                            |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Headers | Helmet with a restrictive Content Security Policy. |

| Area  | Control                                                                           |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Audit | Append only. A Postgres trigger rejects `UPDATE` and `DELETE` on the audit table. |

| Area | Control                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CSRF | Every request with a session that changes state must send `x-orkstage-csrf: 1`. The API allows no CORS from other origins, so a browser on another site cannot send this header. Requests with a bearer API key are exempt. |

| Area | Control                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| OIDC | Authorization code grant with PKCE (S256). `state` and `nonce` are verified. The flow state lives in a signed, short lived cookie. `returnTo` accepts relative paths only. Provider tokens are discarded. |

| `ork targets edit TARGET [--name] [--config KEY=VALUE]... [--credential-ref] [--regions] [--default-region] [--max-concurrent]` | Rotates the role or the credential reference, changes regions or the DNS zone. `KEY=` removes a config key; the account and the state location are fixed. |

| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
